subject: math
title: Numbers to 1000: Place Value, Comparing and Skip Counting
seo_title: Grade 3 Numbers to 1000 Math Worksheets: Free, with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Read, represent, compose, and decompose whole numbers up to and including 1000, using a variety of tools and strategies, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on numbers to 1000 for the Ontario curriculum: base ten blocks, the value of each digit, expanded form, comparing and ordering, and counting by 50s, 100s and 200s. 100 questions with an answer key, good EQAO practice.
key_big: The place of a digit tells you its value. The 4 in 345 is worth 40.
key_sub: Write 0 for an empty place: three hundred five is 305, not 35 or 3005. 346 is 300 + 40 + 6, or 2 hundreds, 14 tens and 6 ones.
body_html:
Hundreds, tens and ones

A 3-digit number has three places: hundreds, tens and ones. 10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. 10 hundreds make 1000.

The value of a digit

The place tells you what a digit is worth.

If a place is empty, write 0 there. The 0 keeps the other digits in the right places.

Write the number

Write “three hundred five” as a number.

3 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones. Write 3, 0, 5.

Answer: 305 (not 35 or 3005)

Expanded form and decomposing

Expanded form shows the value of each digit: 346 = 300 + 40 + 6. You can also decompose a number another way. Trade 1 hundred for 10 tens.

Decompose

Decompose 346 in two ways.

3 hundreds, 4 tens and 6 ones. Or 2 hundreds, 14 tens and 6 ones.

Answer: 300 + 40 + 6 = 200 + 140 + 6

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 3-digit number is greater than a 2-digit number. If both have 3 digits, compare the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones.

Compare

452 ☐ 425

Hundreds: 4 = 4. Tens: 5 tens > 2 tens.

Answer: 452 > 425

> means “is greater than”. < means “is less than”. The open side faces the greater number.

Count by 50s, 100s and 200s

Counting by 50s: 50, 100, 150, 200 … Two 50s make 100. Counting by 100s changes only the hundreds digit: 230, 330, 430. Counting by 200s: 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing each part you hear (three hundred five = 3005)A number in the hundreds has 3 digits: 305
Leaving out the zero (305 = 35)Write 0 for the empty tens place: 305
Reading the digit, not its value (the 4 in 345 is 4)The 4 is in the tens place: 40
Writing 14 tens inside the number (2 hundreds, 14 tens, 6 ones = 2146)14 tens = 140, so 200 + 140 + 6 = 346
Comparing the first digits only (98 > 102)Count the digits first: 102 > 98
Thinking every mark on a number line is 1 or 100Work out the jump first: 0 to 500 in 10 jumps means 50 each

faq.q: What number skills are in the Grade 3 Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 3 students read, represent, compose and decompose whole numbers up to 1000 (B1.1), compare and order them (B1.2), count to 1000 by 50s, 100s and 200s (B1.4) and explain the value of each digit (B1.5).
Base ten blocks are the place value materials used in Ontario classrooms: a small cube is 1, a rod is 10 and a flat is 100. Ten flats make 1000, so children can see what each digit is worth.

faq.q: Why is zero important in place value?
faq.a: Zero holds an empty place so the other digits keep their value. Without it, 305 would become 35, so children learn to write 0 when there are no tens or no ones.

faq.q: Is place value on the Grade 3 EQAO math test?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 3 EQAO math assessment follows the Ontario curriculum, and the Number strand includes reading, comparing and decomposing numbers to 1000.

sets.title: Base ten blocks: hundreds, tens and ones

items.e: A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 hundreds, 3 tens and 4 ones make 234. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 5 tens and 2 ones make 152. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 hundreds, 2 tens and 6 ones make 326. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
Each rod is 1 ten. There are 5 rods, so there are 5 tens. The number is 352.
Each flat is 1 hundred. There are 4 flats, so there are 4 hundreds. The number is 426.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 2 hundreds, 8 tens and 5 ones make 285. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 4 hundreds, 1 ten and 7 ones make 417. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
Count each kind: 3 flats, 6 rods, 4 small cubes. That is 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 4 ones: 364.
Count each kind: 2 flats, 5 rods, 7 small cubes. That is 2 hundreds, 5 tens and 7 ones: 257.
Each small cube is 1 one. There are 8 cubes, so there are 8 ones. The number is 278.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 1 hundred, 7 tens and 9 ones make 179. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 1 one make 341. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
Count each kind: 5 flats, 1 rod, 8 small cubes. That is 5 hundreds, 1 ten and 8 ones: 518.

items.q: Which number has 4 hundreds, 2 tens and 9 ones?
items.e: Write the hundreds digit first, then the tens, then the ones: 4, 2, 9. That is 429.
A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a small cube is 1. 5 hundreds, 6 tens and 3 ones make 563. Start with the flats, then the rods, then the small cubes.
The blocks show 245. A rod is 10. 245 + 10 = 255. Only the tens digit changes.
The blocks show 136. A flat is 100. 136 + 100 = 236. Only the hundreds digit changes.
The blocks show 359. Add 1 cube: now there are 10 cubes. Trade 10 cubes for 1 rod. That is 3 hundreds, 6 tens and 0 ones: 360.

items.q: Which number has 7 hundreds, 3 tens and 1 one?
items.e: Write the hundreds digit first, then the tens, then the ones: 7, 3, 1. That is 731.
Each flat is 100. Count by 100s: 100, 200, 300 … 1000. 10 hundreds make 1000.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 4 is in the tens place. It is worth 4 tens = 40. The digit is 4, but its value is 40.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 5 is in the hundreds place. It is worth 5 hundreds = 500. The digit is 5, but its value is 500.

items.q: What is the value of the 7 in 473?
items.e: The 7 is in the tens place. It is worth 7 tens = 70. The digit is 7, but its value is 70.

items.q: In 736, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 736 is 7 hundreds, 3 tens and 6 ones. The hundreds digit is 7. (Its value is 700.)

items.q: Write “three hundred five” as a number.
items.e: Three hundred five is 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones: 305. Write 0 for the empty tens place. The 0 keeps the other digits in the right places.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 6 is in the ones place. It is worth 6 ones = 6.

items.q: Which number has a 6 in the tens place?
items.e: 263 is 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 3 ones. The 6 is in the tens place.

items.q: What is the value of the 6 in 619?
items.e: The 6 is in the hundreds place. It is worth 6 hundreds = 600. The digit is 6, but its value is 600.

items.q: How many tens are in 507?
items.e: 507 is 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. The 0 shows there are no tens.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 9 is in the tens place. It is worth 9 tens = 90. The digit is 9, but its value is 90.

items.q: Write “four hundred six” as a number.
items.e: Four hundred six is 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones: 406. Write 0 for the empty tens place. The 0 keeps the other digits in the right places.

items.q: In 418, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 418 is 4 hundreds, 1 ten and 8 ones. The tens digit is 1. (Its value is 10.)

items.q: Which number has an 8 in the hundreds place?
items.e: 815 is 8 hundreds, 1 ten and 5 ones. The 8 is in the hundreds place.

items.q: What is the value of the 8 in 538?
items.e: The 8 is in the ones place. It is worth 8 ones = 8.

items.q: Which number has 0 tens?
items.e: 306 is 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones. 360 and 630 have 0 ones, and 36 has 3 tens.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 2 is in the hundreds place. It is worth 2 hundreds = 200. The digit is 2, but its value is 200.

items.q: Write “eight hundred seventy” as a number.
items.e: Eight hundred seventy is 8 hundreds, 7 tens and 0 ones: 870. Write 0 for the empty ones place. The 0 keeps the other digits in the right places.

items.q: Which number has a 3 in the ones place?
items.e: 473 is 4 hundreds, 7 tens and 3 ones. The 3 is in the ones place.

items.q: What is the value of the 2 in 924?
items.e: The 2 is in the tens place. It is worth 2 tens = 20. The digit is 2, but its value is 20.

items.q: The CN Tower in Toronto is 553 m tall. What is the value of the 5 in the tens place?
items.e: 553 is 5 hundreds, 5 tens and 3 ones. The 5 in the tens place is worth 50. The other 5 is in the hundreds place and is worth 500.

items.q: What is 346 in expanded form?
items.e: 346 is 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 6 ones. That is 300 + 40 + 6.

items.q: What is 572 in expanded form?
items.e: 572 is 5 hundreds, 7 tens and 2 ones. That is 500 + 70 + 2.

items.q: 300 + ☐ + 6 = 346. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 346 is 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 6 ones. 4 tens = 40.

items.q: ☐ + 20 + 9 = 829. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 829 is 8 hundreds, 2 tens and 9 ones. 8 hundreds = 800.

items.q: How do you write 708 in words?
items.e: 708 is 7 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones. Say the hundreds, then the ones: seven hundred eight.

items.q: What is 508 in expanded form?
items.e: 508 is 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 8 ones. 0 tens adds nothing. So 508 = 500 + 8.

items.q: What is 690 in expanded form?
items.e: 690 is 6 hundreds, 9 tens and 0 ones. 9 tens = 90. So 690 = 600 + 90.

items.q: What number is 600 + 7?
items.e: 600 + 7 is 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones: 607. Do not write 600 and then 7. The answer has only 3 digits.

items.q: 400 + ☐ = 407. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 407 is 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. 400 + 7 = 407.

items.q: 600 + 30 + ☐ = 635. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 635 is 6 hundreds, 3 tens and 5 ones. The ones part is 5.

items.q: How do you write 350 in words?
items.e: 350 is 3 hundreds, 5 tens and 0 ones. 5 tens is fifty, not fifteen: three hundred fifty.

items.q: What number is 400 + 90?
items.e: 400 + 90 is 4 hundreds, 9 tens and 0 ones: 490. Do not write 400 and then 90. The answer has only 3 digits.
There are 14 rods. 10 rods make 1 hundred, so 14 tens = 1 hundred and 4 tens. 200 + 140 + 6 = 346.

items.q: 346 = 2 hundreds, ☐ tens and 6 ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: Take 1 hundred from 3 hundreds and make it 10 tens. Now there are 2 hundreds and 10 + 4 = 14 tens. Check: 200 + 140 + 6 = 346.

items.q: What number do the base ten blocks show?
items.e: 15 small cubes are 1 ten and 5 ones. 300 + 15 = 315.

items.q: 523 = 4 hundreds, 12 tens and ☐ ones. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 4 hundreds = 400 and 12 tens = 120. 400 + 120 = 520. 523 − 520 = 3. So there are 3 ones.

items.q: Which is another way to make 346?
items.e: 2 hundreds = 200 and 14 tens = 140. 200 + 140 + 6 = 346. (The others make 246, 446 and 356.)

items.q: Which is not equal to 250?
430 = ☐ tens. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 430 = 4 hundreds and 3 tens. 4 hundreds = 40 tens. 40 + 3 = 43 tens. Check: 43 × 10 = 430.

items.q: 357 = 200 + ☐ + 7. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 357 = 300 + 50 + 7. Only 200 is used, so 100 moves to the tens part: 100 + 50 = 150. Check: 200 + 150 + 7 = 357.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens: 5 tens is more than 2 tens. So 452 > 425.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens: 9 tens is more than 0 tens. So 390 > 309.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens: 4 tens is more than 3 tens. So 543 > 534. 543 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 86 is the only number with 2 digits, so it is the least, even though 8 is a big digit.

items.q: Put 271, 217 and 712 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: Hundreds first: 712 has 7 hundreds, so it is the greatest. 217 and 271 both have 2 hundreds. Tens: 1 ten < 7 tens, so 217 < 271. Order: 217, 271, 712.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 102 has 3 digits and 98 has only 2. So 102 > 98. Do not just look at the first digit: count the digits first.

items.q: Use the digits 4, 7 and 2 once each. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the hundreds place, then the next biggest: 7, 4, 2. That is 742.

items.q: Which number is between 450 and 500?
items.e: A number between 450 and 500 is greater than 450 and less than 500. 476 has 4 hundreds and 7 tens, so it fits. 445 is too small. 504 and 540 are too big.

items.q: Put 450, 405 and 45 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 45 has only 2 digits, so it is the least. 405 and 450 both have 4 hundreds. Tens: 0 tens < 5 tens, so 405 < 450. Order: 45, 405, 450.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens: 7 tens is more than 0 tens. So 670 > 607.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 1000 has 4 digits. 999, 990 and 909 have only 3. 1000 is 1 more than 999, so 1000 is the greatest.

items.q: Use the digits 5, 0 and 3 once each. What is the least 3-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 3-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest other digit first: 3. Then 0, then 5: 305. (035 is just 35, which has only 2 digits.)

items.q: Put 836, 863 and 638 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 638 has only 6 hundreds, so it is the least. 836 and 863 both have 8 hundreds. Tens: 6 tens > 3 tens, so 863 > 836. Order: 863, 836, 638.

items.q: What number is 10 less than 600?
items.e: 10 less than 600: count back one ten. 600 is 60 tens, and 1 ten less is 59 tens = 590. 500 is 100 less, and 610 is 10 more.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1000 has 4 digits and 999 has only 3. So 1000 > 999.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: All have 7 hundreds. Tens: 702 has 0 tens, which is the fewest. So 702 is the least.

items.q: Which number is between 700 and 750?
items.e: 728 has 7 hundreds and 2 tens, so it is between 700 and 750. 782 and 770 are more than 750. 699 is less than 700.

items.q: Put 529, 592, 925 and 259 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: Hundreds: 2 < 5 < 9, so 259 is the least and 925 is the greatest. 529 and 592 both have 5 hundreds: 2 tens < 9 tens. Order: 259, 529, 592, 925.

items.q: Use the digits 8, 0 and 6 once each. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Biggest digit first: 8. Then 6. The 0 goes last, in the ones place: 860.

items.q: Put 1000, 100, 910 and 190 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: 1000 has 4 digits, so it is the greatest. Then compare the hundreds: 9 > 1, so 910 comes next. 190 > 100 because 9 tens > 0 tens. Order: 1000, 910, 190, 100.

sets.title: Count by 50s, 100s and 200s, number lines and word problems

items.q: Count by 50s: 350, 400, 450, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Count by 50s: each number is 50 more. 450 + 50 = 500. (460 is counting by 10s.)

items.q: Count by 100s: 230, 330, 430, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Count by 100s: only the hundreds digit changes. 4 hundreds → 5 hundreds: 530.

items.q: Count by 200s: 200, 400, 600, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Count by 200s: each number is 200 more. 600 + 200 = 800. (700 is counting by 100s.)

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 1000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 100. The arrow is 3 marks after 500: 600, 700, 800.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 500 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 50, not 100. The arrow is 3 marks after 500: 550, 600, 650.

items.q: Count back by 50s: 900, 850, 800, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Count back by 50s: each number is 50 less. 800 − 50 = 750.

items.q: Count back by 100s: 950, 850, 750, ☐. What comes next?
items.e: Count back by 100s: the hundreds digit goes down by 1. 7 hundreds → 6 hundreds: 650.

items.q: Lucas counts by 200s. He starts at 0 and makes 4 jumps. Where does he land?
items.e: Each jump is 200: 200, 400, 600, 800. After 4 jumps Lucas lands on 800.

items.q: The jumps start at 300. Each jump is 50. Where does the 4th jump land?
items.e: Count by 50s from 300: 350, 400, 450, 500. The 4th jump lands on 500.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 500 to 750 there are 5 jumps, so each mark is 50. The arrow is 3 marks after 750: 800, 850, 900.

items.q: Canada geese fly in groups of 50. Mateo counts 6 groups. How many geese is that?
Zoe counts money from the Terry Fox Run: three $100 bills, four $10 bills and two loonies. How much money is that?
items.e: Three $100 bills = $300. Four $10 bills = $40. Two loonies = $2. $300 + $40 + $2 = $342.

items.q: The hockey arena has “eight hundred six” seats. Write the number of seats.
items.e: Eight hundred six is 8 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones: 806. Write 0 for the empty tens place.

items.q: The Martin farm made 450 L of maple syrup. The Roy farm made 540 L. Which farm made more?
items.e: Compare the hundreds: 5 hundreds > 4 hundreds. So 540 > 450. The Roy farm made more.

items.q: Pencils come in boxes of 10. The school buys 36 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: 36 tens = 3 hundreds and 6 tens = 360. 30 boxes is 300 pencils. 6 more boxes is 60. 300 + 60 = 360.

items.q: Paper comes in packs of 200 sheets. The teacher has 4 packs. How many sheets is that?
items.e: Count by 200s: 200, 400, 600, 800. 4 packs of 200 = 800 sheets.

items.q: Three schools go on a field trip. Maple Grove sends 316 students, Lakeview sends 361 and Pine Ridge sends 136. Which list goes from least to greatest?
items.e: 136 has only 1 hundred, so it is the least. 316 and 361 both have 3 hundreds. Tens: 1 ten < 6 tens. Order: 136, 316, 361.

items.q: Chloe’s mystery number is between 600 and 700. It has 5 tens and 0 ones. What is it?
items.e: Between 600 and 700 means 6 hundreds. Then 5 tens and 0 ones: 650.

items.q: For the food drive, Nathan stacks cans in groups of 50. There are 9 groups. How many cans is that?
items.e: Count by 50s: 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450. 9 groups of 50 = 450 cans. (Two groups of 50 make 100, so 8 groups make 400, and 1 more group makes 450.)

items.q: For Canada Day, a town buys flags in boxes of 100. It buys 10 boxes. How many flags is that?
items.e: Count by 100s: 100, 200, 300 … 1000. 10 hundreds make 1000 flags. (110 is 100 + 10, but the town has 10 boxes of 100.)
